lines.text: Can one can of spray make a bucket that was sawn in half hold water?
Flex Seal is the only one of three that actually holds the water.
Because it goes on thick enough to bridge the gap like a rubber skin instead of just coating the edges.
beats: ai:thick black rubber coating stretching across a crack in white plastic macro bright light sharp focus

lines.text: But on a cracked pipe underwater Rust-Oleum holds all the way to 43 psi.
That's about the water pressure in your house.
beats: ai:a kitchen faucet running at full pressure into a steel sink bright daylight sharp focus

lines.text: And Flex Seal scrapes right off the smooth PVC because it barely bonds to slick plastic.
beats: ai:a black rubber coating peeling off smooth white plastic pipe macro bright light sharp focus

lines.text: On a metal tank Flex Seal starts leaking at just 2 psi.
That's less pressure than you blow into a balloon so it fills gaps well but it doesn't stick to everything.
beats: ai:a person blowing up a red balloon in a bright room sharp focus

lines.text: In the end Flex Seal and Rust-Oleum tie with two wins each so the TV hype is only half true.
Would you trust it on your roof?
